### [Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation](https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-agent-skills-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-22

Anthropic is donating the open-standard Agent Skills project—including its domain, GitHub organization, and trademarks—to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation.

- Agent Skills is an open standard defined by a folder containing a SKILL.md file alongside relevant scripts and reference material to supply domain-specific procedural knowledge.
- Anthropic is transferring ownership of the agentskills.io domain, logo, name, and GitHub organization to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).
- Individual engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other firms will maintain the specification, led by David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag.
- The standard is currently integrated into over 70 platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and VS Code, with 1 million skills published.
- The initial AAIF roadmap will introduce versioned releases, a formal proposal process, and security guidelines for skill authors and users.

**Why it matters:** Transferring the Agent Skills specification to a neutral foundation prevents single-vendor lock-in and provides a standardized format for procedural knowledge across diverse AI platforms.

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-22

Anthropic has donated its Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), an open, vendor-neutral organization under the Linux Foundation.

- Anthropic transferred ownership of the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).
- AAIF operates under the Linux Foundation and was co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI.

### [Open call for guest investigators in the life sciences](https://www.anthropic.com/news/open-call-guest-investigators-life-sciences)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-22

Anthropic is inviting principal investigators from academia, nonprofits, or government labs to apply for 8–12 week collaborative research projects using Claude.

- Target research domains include causal human biology, structural/computational molecular biology, medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, and clinical science.
- Anthropic provides direct collaboration with its researchers and runs its models and harnesses at no cost to selected applicants.
- Outputs must be deliverable within 8–12 weeks, with results published and accompanying data and code open-sourced.
- Guest investigators retain full rights to their data and any independent follow-on research.

**Why it matters:** Domain experts gain free access to Anthropic's compute models and technical team to accelerate life sciences discoveries and create open-source computational tools.
